sentences.en: In the last few weeks, we've been looking at various aspects of the social history of London, and this morning we're continuing with a look at life in the area called the East End.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几周里，我们一直在探讨伦敦社会史的各个方面，而今天上午我们将继续关注被称为‘东区’（East End）这一地区的居民生活。

sentences.en: I'll start with a brief history of the district, and then focus on life in the first half of the twentieth century.
sentences.zh: 我将首先简要介绍该地区的历史，然后重点讲述20世纪上半叶的生活状况。

sentences.en: Back in the first to the fourth centuries AD, when the Romans controlled England, London grew into a town of 45,000 people, and what's now the East End - the area by the river Thames, and along the road heading north-east from London to the coast - consisted of farmland with crops and livestock which helped to feed that population.
sentences.zh: 早在公元1至4世纪罗马人统治英格兰时期，伦敦已发展为一座拥有4.5万人口的城镇；而如今的东区——即泰晤士河沿岸、以及从伦敦向东北通往海岸的道路沿线区域——当时主要是农田，种植作物并饲养牲畜，用以供养该城镇人口。

sentences.en: www.TopSage.com Tapescripts } SLA8 The Romans left in 410, at the beginning of the fifth century, and from then onwards the country suffered a series of invasions by tribes from present-day Germany and DenmarkAQC.com the Angles, Saxons and Jutes, many of whom settled in the East End.
sentences.zh: www.TopSage.com 录音稿 } SLA8 罗马人于公元410年、即5世纪初撤离，此后英国接连遭受来自今德国和丹麦一带部落——盎格鲁人、撒克逊人与朱特人——的入侵，其中许多人定居于东区。

sentences.en: The technology they introduced meant that metal and leather goods were produced there for the first time.
sentences.zh: 他们所引入的技术使得金属制品与皮革制品首次在当地得以生产。

sentences.en: And as 032 the East End was by the river, ships could transport goods between there and foreign markets.
sentences.zh: 而且由于东区毗邻河流，船只可在此与海外市场之间运输货物。

sentences.en: In the eleventh century, in 1066 to be precise, the Normans conquered England, and during the next few centuries London became one of the most powerful and prosperous cities in Europe.
sentences.zh: 11世纪时，确切地说是1066年，诺曼人征服了英格兰；在随后几个世纪中，伦敦逐渐成为欧洲最强大、最繁荣的城市之一。

sentences.en: The East End benefited from this, and because there were fewer restrictions there than in the city itself, plenty of newcomers settled there from abroad, bringing their skills as workers, merchants or money-lenders during the next few hundred years.
sentences.zh: 东区由此受益；又因当地对人口迁入的限制比伦敦城区本身更少，故此后数百年间，大量海外新移民纷纷在此定居，带来了工匠、商人或放贷人的专业技能。

sentences.en: In the sixteenth century the first dock was dug where ships were constructed, eventually making the East End the focus of massive international trade.
sentences.zh: 16世纪时，首个船坞在此开挖，用于建造船舶，最终使东区成为大规模国际贸易的核心区域。

sentences.en: And in the late sixteenth century, when much of the rest of England was suffering economically, a lot of agricultural workers came to the East End to look for alternative work.
sentences.zh: 16世纪晚期，当英格兰大部分地区正经历经济困境时，许多农业工人涌入东区，寻求替代性工作机会。

sentences.en: In the seventeenth century, the East End was still a series of separate, semi-rural settlements.
sentences.zh: 17世纪时，东区仍由一系列彼此分离、半乡村性质的聚居点组成。

sentences.en: There was a shortage of accommodation, so marshland was drained and built on to house 036 the large numbers of people now living there.
sentences.zh: 当时住房严重短缺，因此人们排干沼泽地并在其上建房，以容纳日益增多的居民。

sentences.en: By the nineteenth century London was the busiest port in the world, and this became the main source of employment in the East End.
sentences.zh: 至19世纪，伦敦已成为全球最繁忙的港口，这也成为东区最主要的就业来源。

sentences.en: Those who could afford to live in more pleasant surroundings moved out, and the arca became one where the vast majority of people lived in extreme poverty, and suffered from appalling sanitary conditions.
sentences.zh: 那些有能力居住在更宜人环境中的居民纷纷搬离，该地区遂演变为绝大多数人深陷极端贫困、并饱受恶劣卫生条件之苦的区域。

sentences.en: That brief outline takes us to the beginning of the twentieth century, and now we'll turn to housing.
sentences.zh: 以上简要概述将我们带至20世纪初，接下来我们将转向住房问题。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the century, living conditions for the majority of working people in East London were very basic indeed.
sentences.zh: 世纪之初，东伦敦大多数劳动者的居住条件确实极为简陋。

sentences.en: Houses were crowded closely together and usually very 038/39/40 badly built, because there was no regulation.
sentences.zh: 房屋密集排列，且通常建造质量极差，因为当时尚无相关监管法规。

sentences.en: But the poor and needy were attracted by the possibility of work, and they had to be housed.
sentences.zh: 然而，贫困与弱势群体被就业机会所吸引而来，他们必须获得住所。

sentences.en: It was the availability, rather than the condition, of the housing that was the major concern for tenants and landlords alike.
sentences.zh: 对租户与房东而言，住房供应是否充足，远比其实际状况更为重要。

sentences.en: Few houses had electricity at this time, so other sources of power were used, like coal for /39140 the fires which heated perhaps just one room.
sentences.zh: 当时极少有住宅通电，因而人们普遍使用其他能源，例如煤炭——仅用于加热可能唯一的一间房间的炉火。

sentences.en: Of course, the smoke from these contributed a great deal to the air pollution for which London used to be famous.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些炉火产生的烟雾极大加剧了伦敦昔日闻名于世的空气污染问题。

sentences.en: A tiny, damp, unhealthy house like this might well be occupied by two full families, possibly 238/39/40 including several children, grandparents, aunts and uncles.
sentences.zh: 像这样狭小、潮湿、不健康的房屋，往往同时住着两个完整的家庭，其中很可能包括多名儿童、祖父母、姑姨叔舅等亲属。

sentences.en: Now, before go on to health implications of this way of life, I'll say something about food and nutrition.
sentences.zh: 现在，在进一步探讨这种生活方式对健康的影响之前，我先简要谈谈食物与营养问题。
